newsitem.title: GERMANY: German M3, Ifo to point to modest recovery - analysts.
newsitem.headline: German M3, Ifo to point to modest recovery - analysts.

text.p: German money supply and the business climate among companies in August are likely to show the German economy on course for a modest recovery with no near-term inflation pressures, analysts said Monday.
Both the August data on money supply M3 and the latest business climate index from the Munich-based Ifo Institute for Economic Research are expected from Thursday onward.

Most economists predict M3 growth slowed to an annualised rate of 8.0 percent from 8.6 percent in July. Forecasts ranged from 7.9 percent to 8.2 percent. The Bundesbank is aiming for M3 growth between four and seven percent this year.
But even a stronger-than-expected decline in the aggregate would hardly prompt further easing of monetary policy from the Bundesbank, analysts said.

"Even if M3 does make it into the target corridor by year-end, I don't see any reason to further relax the already expansionist monetary policy," said Irgeen Rust, economist at West-LB in Duesseldorf.
In a research note, Vereinsbank of Munich said there were no price pressures from an oversupply of cash.
"From the Bundesbank's point of view there is no need for action. It is finding its view confirmed that there is no inflation pressure from the monetary side."
Many economists therefore believe that, at least for the time being, the Ifo index is a more significant indicator.

"M3 has become less of a hot topic - the Ifo index is now more important, because it has implications for the strength of the recovery," said Adolf Rosenstock, Senior Economist at Industrial Bank of Japan.

Most analysts predict only a small improvement in western German business sentiment to an index level of around 94.5 for August. In July, the index had posted a stronger-than-expected increase, when it jumped to 94.1 from 90.4 in June.
"Sentiment will continue to strengthen, but at a slower pace than in July," said Gernot Nerb, Senior Economist at Salomon Brothers in London and formerly Ifo's chief economist.

Especially industrial companies should post an improvement in business climate, while retailers may also contribute to a small rise in the index, he said. Sentiment in construction is likely to remain depressed, he added.
However, some economists cautioned that while the business climate should continue to improve in the months ahead, the Ifo index may drop slightly in August in reaction to the strong July figure.
Uwe Angenendt, economist at BHF-Bank said: "The trend should remain upward, but I think we will see a decline in August to 93.0 or 92.5."
